questions.question: If 4 men or 6 boys can finish a piece of work in 20 days, then in how many days can 6 men and 11 boys finish the same work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency Ratio: 4 Men = 6 Boys ⇒ 2 Men = 3 Boys.

Convert Men into Boys: 6 Men = (3 ÷ 2) × 6 = 9 Boys.

Total Group Requirement: 6 Men + 11 Boys = 9 Boys + 11 Boys = 20 Boys.

Using M₁D₁ = M₂D₂ ⇒ 6 Boys × 20 Days = 20 Boys × Days.

Required Days = 120 ÷ 20 = 6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by 4 Men = 20 days ⇒ Time taken by 1 Man = 4 × 20 = 80 days.

Time taken by 6 Boys = 20 days ⇒ Time taken by 1 Boy = 6 × 20 = 120 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual days; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Days.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 1 Man
 80
 240 units
 3 units/day
 
 

 1 Boy
 120
 2 units/day
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of 6 Men = 6 × 3 = 18 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of 11 Boys = 11 × 2 = 22 units/day.

⇒ Combined Efficiency (6 Men + 11 Boys) = 18 + 22 = 40 units/day.

⇒ Required Time = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Required Time = 240 ÷ 40 = 6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Man-Days Formula

The relationship between men, days, and hours is given by (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work (Efficiency ∝ 1 ÷ Time).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by each person, which is the product of efficiency and time.</p

questions.question: Mitu can do a piece of work in 12 hours, Titu and Situ together in 2 hours, and Mitu and Situ together in 3 hours. How long will Titu alone take to do it?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mitu's time to complete the work = 12 hours

Titu and Situ's time together = 2 hours

Mitu and Situ's time together = 3 hours

**Formula used:**

Work done per hour = 1 / Time taken

If A and B work together, their combined work per hour = Work done by A + Work done by B

**Calculations:**

Let Titu's time to complete the work = T hours

Let Situ's time to complete the work = S hours

Mitu's work per hour = 1/12

Titu and Situ's combined work per hour = 1/2

Mitu and Situ's combined work per hour = 1/3

Situ's work per hour:

⇒ 1/S = 1/3 - 1/12

⇒ 1/S = 4/12 - 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4

⇒ S = 4 hours

Titu's work per hour:

⇒ 1/T + 1/4 = 1/2

⇒ 1/T = 1/2 - 1/4

⇒ 1/T = 2/4 - 1/4 = 1/4

⇒ T = 4 hours

**∴ Titu alone will take 4 hours to complete the work.**

questions.question: George can do 35% of the total work in 6 days. Jim and George together completed a piece of work in 12 days. In how many days could Jim, working alone, complete the entire task?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**George** completes 100% work in 6 × (100 / 35) = 120/7 days.

Total Work (LCM of 120/7 and 12) = 120 units.

Efficiency of **George** = 7 and Efficiency of (**Jim** + **George**) = 10.

Efficiency of **Jim** = 10 − 7 = 3 units/day.

Time taken by **Jim** = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Work done by **George** = 35% in 6 days.

Time taken by **Jim** and **George** together = 12 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken by **George** to complete 100% work = 6 ÷ 0.35 = 600/35 = 120/7 days.

⇒ Let the total work be the **LCM** of 120/7 and 12, which is 120 units.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **George**
 120/7
 120
 7
 
 

 **Jim + George**
 12
 10
 
 

⇒ Efficiency of **Jim** = Efficiency of (**Jim** + **George**) − Efficiency of **George**

⇒ Efficiency of **Jim** = 10 − 7 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Time taken by **Jim** alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of **Jim**

⇒ Time taken by **Jim** = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task. If the ratio of time taken by A and B is x:y, then the ratio of their efficiencies is y:x.

Combined Work Rate

If person A takes 'a' days and person B takes 'b' days to complete a task individually, they will complete it together in (a × b) / (a + b) days.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed among workers in the ratio of the total work done by each, which is the product of their individual efficiency and the time they worked.</p

questions.question: Vaibhav can do a piece of work in 60 days. He works there for 15 days and then Sandeep alone finishes the remaining work in 30 days. In how many days will Vaibhav and Sandeep working together finish the work?
questions.solution:
Given:

Vaibhav can do a piece of work = 60 days

Number of days Vaibhav works = 15 days

Sandeep alone finish the remaining work = 30 days

Formula used:

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

Total work = 60

Let efficiency of Sandeep be x, then

15 + 30x = 60

30x = 60 – 15 = 45

x = 45/30 = 1.5

**Vaibhav and Sandeep together can complete the whole work in = 60/(1 + 1.5) = 60/2.5 = 24 days**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Suppose Sandeep can complete the whole work in x days. 

According to the question,

15/60 + 30/x = 1

⇒ 30/x = 1 – 1/4

⇒ 30/x = 3/4

⇒ x = 40 days

Vaibhav and Sandeep together can complete the work in 1 day = 1/60 + 1/40

⇒ (2 + 3)/120 = 5/120 = 1/24

∴ Vaibhav and Sandeep together can complete the whole work in 24 days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Calculation:

Time taken by Vaibhav to complete the work = (60/15) = 4 days

Number of days Sandeep works = (1 – 1/4) = 3/4 days

Time taken by Sandeep to complete the work = (4/3 × 30) = 40 days

Now,

LCM of 60 and 40 is 120

Efficiency of Vaibhav = (120/60) = 2 units/day

Efficiency of Sandeep = (120/40) = 3 units/day

Time taken by Vaibhav and Sandeep together to complete a work = [120/(2 + 3)]

⇒ 120/5 days

⇒ 24 days

∴ The required days is 24 days.

A can complete 3/8 part of a work in 36 days. B can complete 1/2 part of the same work in 27 days. Which of the following statement(s) is are correct?

questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete 3/8 work in 36 days

B can complete 1/2 work in 27 days

Concept: Work efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken.

**Calculation:**

⇒ A's full work will take (36 / 3) × 8 = 96 days.

⇒ B's full work will take (27 / 1) × 2 = 54 days.

I. A is less efficient than B - Correct, since A takes more time than B.

II. A and B working together can complete 11/15 work in 36 days - Incorrect, as working together they can complete (1/96 + 1/54) × 36 = ~0.73 of the work in 36 days.

**Hence, only statement I is correct.**

questions.question: 40 men can complete a work in 15 days. Five days after they started working, 10 more men joined them. In how many days will the total work be completed?
questions.solution:

40 men can complete a work in 15 days

After 5 days 10 more men joined 

**FORMULA USED:**

Total work = No. of men × No. of days 

**CALCULATION:**

One man can do the work in = 40 × 15 = 600 days

One - day work of one man = 1/600 

One- day work of men = ( 1/600 ) × 40 = 1/15 

Now, work done in 5 days = ( 1/15 ) × 5 = 1/3 

Work left = 1 - 1/3 = 2/3 

One- day of work of 50 men = ( 1/600) × 50 = 1/12

Time taken to complete the remaining work = (2/3) × (12/1 ) = 8 days 

Total work done in ( 5 + 8 ) = 13 days.

Hence, number of days taken to complete the total work is 13 days.

Hence total number of days = 8 + 5 = 13 days.

questions.question: A and B can finish a job in 10 days and 5 days, respectively. They worked together for 2 days, after which B was replaced by C and the job was finished in the next 3 days. In how many days will C alone finish 50% of the job?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do a job in 10 days

B can do a job in 5 days

**Concept used:**

Efficiency = Total work/Time taken

**Calculation:**

LCM of 10 and 5 = 10 i.e total work

Efficiency of A = 10/10 = 1 unit/day

Efficiency of B = 10/5 = 2 units/day

Effective efficiency of A and B = 1 + 2 = 3 units/day

A and B work for 2 days

So, work completed = 3 × 2 units

⇒ 6 units

Remaining work = (10 – 6) units

⇒ 4 units

A and C can complete the remaining work in 3 days

So, A and C's one day work = 4/3 units

C's one-day work = (4/3) – 1

⇒ 1/3 unit/day

C can complete 50% of work in (10 × 50\%)/(frac{1){3}} days

⇒ 5 × 3 = 15 days

**∴ C can complete 50% of work in 15 days.**

questions.question: Rama alone can do a work in 5 days working 4 hours a day. Seema alone can do the same work in 3 days working 10 hours a day. How many hours do they need to work together in a day to complete the same work in 6 days?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Rama can finish the work in 5 days working 4 hours a day, that's 5 × 4 = 20 hours.

Seema can finish the work in 3 days working 10 hours a day, that's 3 × 10 = 30 hours.

So, we can say that Rama's work rate is 1/20 of the work per hour, and Seema's work rate is 1/30 of the work per hour.

So, their combined rate is 1/20 + 1/30 = (3 + 2)/60 = 5/60 = 1/12 of the work per hour.

If they want to finish the work in 6 days, and they work together at the combined rate of 1/12 of the work per hour, then they need to work:

6 days × x hours/day = 1 work

x = 1 work / (6 days × 1/12 work/hour)

x = 1 / (6/12) = 2 hours/day

**So, Rama and Seema need to work together for 2 hours each day to finish the work in 6 days.**

**Hence, vikram can do the work in 18 days .**

questions.question: Teena does half of a task in 6 days. Later, with Shyam’s help, she completes the remaining work in 4 days. Shyam alone can finish the entire work in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Teena does half of a task in 6 days.

With Shyam's help, she completes the remaining work in 4 days.

**Formula used:**

Work done by Teena in 6 days = 1/2 of the task.

Work done by Teena in 1 day = 1/12 of the task.

Let Shyam's 1 day work be 1/x of the task.

Combined work done by Teena and Shyam in 4 days = 1/2 of the task.

**Calculation:**

Teena's 1 day work = 1/12

Teena and Shyam's combined 1 day work = 1/4

⇒ 4(Teena's 1 day work + Shyam's 1 day work) = 1/2

⇒ 4(1/12 + 1/x) = 1/2

⇒ 1/12 + 1/x = 1/8

⇒ 1/x = 1/8 - 1/12

⇒ 1/x = (3 - 2)/24

⇒ 1/x = 1/24

Hence, the efficiencies of B and C are 4P and 5P respectively.

Total work = 4 × (P + 4P + 5P) = 40P units

Now, B can do the work alone in = 40P/4P = 10 days

**∴ B alone can do the work in 10 days.**

questions.question: Ruchi, Khushi and Teju can do a piece of work in 30, 40 and 60 days respectively. In how many days can Ruchi do the work, if she is assisted by both Khushi and Teju on every third day?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ruchi can do the work in 30 days

Khushi can do the work in 40 days

Teju can do the work in 60 days

**Formula used:**

Work done = Time taken × Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be 120 units [As LCM of 30, 40, 60 is 120]

So, efficiency of Ruchi, Khushi, Teju = 4, 3, 2

Now,

In 3 days total work completed = 4 + 4 + 9

⇒ 17 units of the work

In 21 days total work completed = 17 × 7

&
;rArr; 119 units

Now remaining 1 unit will complete Ruchi in 1/4 days

So, total time = 21 + 1/4

⇒ (85)/(4) days

**∴ In (85)/(4) days the work will be completed.**
